events.title: CHASING THE LIGHT﻿ – From Paris to the Peloponnese
events.description:
Calloway Fine Art & Consulting is delighted to present the work of artists Bernard Dellario and Jean Schwartz. This latest exhibition explores light, luminosity, and reflections, inviting contemplation and serenity. Chasing The Light beckons viewers to rediscover the beauty of the world through works that capture the City of Light’s unique character and charm, as well as the uniquely sharp, radiant, and transformative light of the Peloponnese. Light has shaped the region’s culture, history, geography, and artistic legacy for millennia. The specific qualities of the Greek sun and atmospheric clarity are widely recognized as fundamental forces in defining the landscape, ancient mythology, architecture, and the emotional resonance of the Mediterranean.

*The gallery is closed on Sundays

events.title: Ghosts of Georgetown & Exorcist Steps Haunted Walking Tour
events.description:
Come along to hear about the ghosts and spirits that still haunt these streets…if you dare.

This is a family-friendly ghost tour through Georgetown to see this exclusive neighborhood’s darker side. Stroll among the historic streets, manicured gardens, and Victorian row houses as you hear stories and deep, dark secrets about DC’s finest neighborhood’s forgotten past. The October 31 tour will include a special haunted light show at the Exorcist steps!

  • We will see one of the most haunted and historic buildings in Washington, DC, the Old Stone House. A pre-Revolutionary home whose original builder may still roam the halls.
  • Look up at old porches painted Haint Blue to keep out the spirits from crossing over the porch. But what if the spirit was already inside?
  • Find out what happened at boarding schools turned hospitals during the American Civil War. Can you still hear the screams of amputations with no sedation?
  • Walk past the historic house whose lights turned off every night at the same time; a nanny’s rules enforced long after her departure.
  • Meet an eccentric man who built stairs to nowhere, slept in a coffin and refused to add electricity to his 1799 home. Hear why one of our guides refuses to lead this tour because he has been stalking her for 10 years, flickering lights when she walks by.
  • End the tour at the Exorcist Stairs, featured in The Exorcist, and hear the true story that inspired a Georgetown student to write the book.

Meet your guide outside 3051 M St NW at the Old Stone House. The tour ends at the top of Exorcist Steps at 36th and Prospect St NW

Tour Duration: 1.5 Hours Walking Tour. Tours are available nightly at 7pm and 8pm.

events.title: Dry Point Printing 2-Day Workshop with Bridget Murphy
events.description:
Explore dry point technique to create your monoprint artwork. In this class we will discuss image composition and combining drawing, texture, and form to create a monoprint of your image.

Students should to bring their sketchbook and multiple images (landscape, still life, portrait, abstract, photograph, etc.) and ideas to review for their first print. Black and white images, preferred. Artwork should be sized to 6×8. Students will be expected to work on their own during the course. No experience necessary.

(Photo courtesy of Washington Printmakers Gallery)

events.title: SOME (So Others Might Eat) Event
events.description:
Sid + Ann Mashburn Shop for Hunger Card event will run Oct. 23 – Oct. 31, 2026. During this exciting, week-long event, in-store shoppers who make a one-time $80 donation to SOME (So Others Might Eat) at the Sid + Ann Mashburn store in Georgetown will receive 20% off nearly everything on their in-store purchases.

SOME, an interfaith, community-based service organization that serves D.C. neighbors experiencing homelessness and poverty, has been the Sid + Ann Mashburn D.C. store nonprofit partner since 2019. Funds raised from the Shop for Hunger Card benefit SOME’s provision of daily emergency services, affordable housing, counseling, substance use disorder treatment, job training, and other crucial services.

events.title: “Ladies of Georgetown” Jewelry Collection
events.description:
Amanda Hagerman Jewelry (3259 Prospect Street NW) is celebrating its first year in Georgetown with a new capsule collection, Ladies of Georgetown. The one-of-a-kind 18K gold jewels are inspired by six extraordinary women who called Georgetown home, including Julia Child, Elizabeth Taylor, Evangeline Bruce, Lorraine Cooper, and The Peters Sisters. Jamie Peva, a Georgetown resident, realtor, and local history enthusiast, helped Amanda bring the stories behind the collection to life. Each piece in the capsule offers a glimpse into one woman’s story and a connection to modern Georgetown. The pieces are on display throughout October and available for purchase.

Hours: Friday / 11am-5pm; Saturday / 11am – 6pm; Sunday / 11am – 3pm

(Photo courtesy of Amanda Hagerman Jewelry)
